full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Mohammad Ziaul Karim, J:  This Rule Nisi was issued, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the exclusion/cancellation of the petitioner's recommendation by the PSC for appointment to the BCS (Admn.) Cadre, as published in the Daily Prothom Alo on 2nd February, 2005 (Annexure-A), should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that in response to a public advertisement by the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (PSC), the petitioner, applied for 24th BCS examination on 09-11-2002. In the application, he indicated that his father Md. Abdul Matin was a freedom fighter. The petitioner was duly registered under no.82394 and accordingly an admit card was issued to him. Thereafter, he appeared in the successive examinations. Finally, on the basis of his total result, he was recommended for BCS(Admn) Cadre along with 349 others and the said result was published at page 13 at serial no.301 of the Daily Prothom Alo dated 2'd February 2005 (Annexure-A). The name of the petitioner's father Md. Abdul Matin was finally published in the notification dated 04.09.2003, which was also published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extra-Ordinary on 04.12.2004 at serial no.1071, page-80I9 (Annexure-B). Subsequently, a Provisional Certificate being no. M 85018 dated 18-04-2005 was issued to the petitioner's father as a Muktijoddha by the State Minister-in- Charge of the ministry of Muktijoddha Affairs. Eventually, the final result recommending the petitioner for an appointment to the BCS (Admn) Cadre was published in the daily newspaper on 02,02.2005. But long before the said date, the name of the petitioner's father was included in the notification dated 04-09-'2003 and in the Official Gazette on 04-12- 2004. After publication of the final recommendation by the PSC including the petitioner for appointment in the BCS(Admn) Cadre, the petitioner was awaiting for his appointment. As the mater was delayed, then he approached to the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment and also to the respondent no.2 but with no effect (Annexure-C). Lastly the petitioner served a notice demanding justice to the respondents for his appointment (Annexure-D) but the justice was denied. 

 5. Mr. Abdur Rab Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner seeks to impeach the impugned order on the two fold arguments. At the first instance, it is stressed that the petitioner having successfully completed all the formalities of the PSC and the PSC finally recommended his case for having to the BCS(Admn) Cadre, the petitioner had acquired a valuable right for consideration for appointment and his execution without any reason is violative of the fundamental rights guaranteed in Article 29(1) of the Constitution. Secondly, he submits that the, PSC having accepted his testimonial as a son of the freedom fighter and having not asked him to submit his final certificate issued by the Ministry of Freedom Fighter Affairs, the PSC was not within his legal rights to exclude the petitioner without affording him an opportunity to produce his certificate, which was issued after his Viva-voce on 13-10-2004. The learned Counsel lastly submits the Government is a Government by law and it cannot act in an arbitrary and malafide manner, but the same was done in case of the petitioner and as such the impugned action is required to be declared as illegal and without lawful authority. 

 11. In the advertisement for 24th BCS examination, 2002 dated 12-09-2002 which was subsequently published in Bangladesh Gazette dated 14-11-2002 Annexure 1b to Affidavit in opposition dated 23-03-2007, filed by respondent no.2, at Clause 7, criteria for submitting application has been prescribed. For the convenience of understanding Clause-7 of the advertisement (Atinxure-1 b) reads as hereunder: 

 13. The candidates who failed to produce the relevant Certificate at the time of Viva Voice examination, their provisional result also published in the shape of press release, wherein the name of the petitioner was included in the administrative cadre. But in the press release (Annexure- 1 e) it was also clearly stated that:- 

 20. On careful consideration of the report (Annexure-2), and the documents attached with it, we find that all the witnesses in one voice stated that Md. Abdul Matin is the son of late Yeas in Munshi. Surprisingly, the petitioner Md. Nazrul Islam himself categorically stated that his grand father's name is late Haji Yeasin Munshi, but in the Muktijoddha Gazette his name was wrongly published as late Ahammad Ali. Therefore we find that the Certificate (Annexure-F) attached with the supplementary affidavit dated 07-05-2007 itself contradicts with the statement of the petitioner and as such the same are vulnerable to the credibility.
